operator_io_quirks: Mixed-case identifiers: tables Activity/Participates_in/Faculty_Participates_in/Student/Faculty; columns StuID, LName, Fname, FacID, actid, city_code — case-insensitive lookup + double-quoted output required.
FK child column spelled 'FacID' (Faculty_Participates_in) vs parent 'FacID' (Faculty) — case differs from 'stuid'/'StuID' pattern; pragma FK list gives parent_col explicitly.
FK child 'stuid' -> parent 'Student.StuID': child lowercase, parent mixed case; must match case-insensitively when resolving parent column.
Participates_in and Faculty_Participates_in have NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
All columns notnull=0, no CHECK, no UNIQUE indexes — nothing to enforce; TS insert failures unlikely here.
DDL has tabs inside Faculty column defs ('FacID\t       INTEGER') — line-based unique/check scan must tolerate whitespace.
Tiny tables (16/70/40/34/58 rows) — original_values fully read, no rowid sampling needed; original_sizes exact.
Activity.actid samples start at 770 (not 1) — PK values are non-contiguous, non-sequential; fresh PKs from Number fuzzer will be far from originals.
Student.Advisor values (1121, 7712, 7792, 8423) look like Faculty.FacID but there is NO declared FK — TS treats Advisor as plain Number, not FK.
Student.Major values (600,520,540,550,100) are department codes, no FK — plain Number.
Faculty.Phone INTEGER but semantically a phone number (2424,3593) — Number fuzzer will produce arbitrary ints, not phone-shaped.
Room values mix numeric and alphanumeric ('224','224B') stored as text — String fuzzer, VARCHAR(5) length cap not enforced by sqlite.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on all INTEGER columns (actid, StuID, FacID, Age, Major, Advisor, Phone, stuid): range [-10^0,10^0] default scale=0 -> ints in [-1,1] perturbed, OR list-range from 5 sampled originals; produces implausible ages/IDs far from 18-26 or 1001-3457.

String fuzzer on VARCHAR(n) columns: length range from sampled originals, CHARSET a-zA-Z0-9() — names become random strings, Sex becomes multi-char garbage (VARCHAR(1) not enforced), city_code loses 3-letter shape.
Sex VARCHAR(1) with 2 distinct values (F/M): String fuzzer will emit random strings, breaking 'Sex=F' predicates -> likely FN (no rows match) and FP (garbage matches nothing but joins still work).
Rank VARCHAR(15) 4 distinct (Instructor/Professor/AssocProf/AsstProf): String fuzzer randomizes -> 'Rank=Professor' queries return empty -> FN.
Building 3 distinct (NEB/Barton/Krieger): same randomization -> FN on Building predicates.

FK columns (Participates_in.stuid/actid, Faculty_Participates_in.FacID/actid) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates and ties preserved, good for join/aggregate queries; but parent PK filtering may shrink parent below child size -> many duplicate FK values.

Activity.actid PK: single-column PK -> max_l0=inf, so fresh PKs never reused -> 16 distinct fresh actids, but child FK draws from these 16 -> joins still work; original actids (770+) never appear -> queries with literal actid=770 return empty -> FN.
Student.StuID PK fresh values in [-1,1] range (scale=0) -> tiny ints, collide with nothing; Advisor/Major also tiny -> 'Advisor=1121' FN.
No NOT NULL/CHECK -> no insert failures; all rows land, so row counts match chosen sizes (up to 2500) — good for COUNT queries but sizes differ from original 16-70.

Empty PK tables (Participates_in) get full random rows with FK-consistent values -> join cardinality plausible; but no dedup -> duplicate (stuid,actid) pairs possible, affecting DISTINCT/COUNT(DISTINCT) queries.
Age INTEGER scale=0 -> values in [-1,1] perturbed, so 'Age>20' returns empty (FN) and 'Age<20' returns all (FP on selectivity).
